claims.text: Controlled DSC can be used to estimate melting temperatures across single-phase high-entropy alloys.
DSC data can be used to determine fusion enthalpy and entropy in high-entropy alloys.
Lever-rule analysis of DSC data can determine the volume change at melting.
Integrating DSC and lever-rule analysis with CALPHAD can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method will agree with independent measurements within approximately 5–10%.
Arc melting and additive manufacturing can prepare homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy-alloy samples suitable for this method.
Conducting DSC under inert conditions from below the solidus to above melting minimizes kinetic effects and supercooling.
Configurational entropy stabilizes the single-phase solid solution in high-entropy alloys.
Configurational entropy produces distinct thermal signatures at the onset of melting.
The measured heat capacity rises dramatically when the solidus temperature is reached.
Lever-rule analysis of thermal-expansion or DSC curves permits phase-fraction deconvolution during melting.
Correlating the deconvolved thermal response with CALPHAD predictions enables extraction of melting temperature, latent heat, entropy change, and volume change.
Melting temperature is governed by the relative fusion enthalpy and fusion entropy.
The proposed DSC and CALPHAD workflow is efficient and reliable.
Similar DSC-based methods combined with CALPHAD have proven effective in simpler metallic systems.
Previous high-entropy-alloy studies using lever-rule analysis have achieved comparable performance.
The method is primarily applicable to confirmed homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Significant multiphase behavior or chemical inhomogeneity compromises the accuracy of the method.
Overlapping thermal signals caused by secondary phases or local compositional variation can increase uncertainty beyond 10%.
Failure for a majority of tested single-phase alloys by deviations exceeding approximately 10% would rule out the proposed method.
